questions.prompt: What does self-attention compute, in contrast to the cross-attention covered in the NLP course?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: How each element in a sequence relates to every other element within that same sequence, rather than between two different sequences

Self-attention applies the attention mechanism within a single sequence — each element attends to every other element in the same sequence — as opposed to cross-attention, which relates two different sequences to each other, like a decoder attending to an encoder's output.
keyPoints: Self-attention applies the attention mechanism within a single sequence — each element attends to every other element in the same sequence — as opposed to cross-attention, which relates two different sequences to each other, like a decoder attending to an encoder's output.

questions.prompt: Why might a single attention computation be insufficient for capturing everything relevant in language?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: Language relationships come in many different flavors simultaneously (syntax, semantics, coreference), and asking one attention computation to capture all of them at once is a real limitation

Since language involves many different kinds of relationships between words happening at once, having only one attention computation forces it to try to capture all of these simultaneously — multi-head attention instead gives the model room to potentially specialize.
keyPoints: Since language involves many different kinds of relationships between words happening at once, having only one attention computation forces it to try to capture all of these simultaneously — multi-head attention instead gives the model room to potentially specialize.

questions.prompt: How is the feed-forward sublayer applied across a sequence, in contrast to self-attention?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: It's applied independently and identically to each position, using the same learned weights, without mixing information between different positions

Unlike self-attention, which explicitly relates different positions to each other, the feed-forward sublayer transforms each position's representation on its own, applying the exact same learned weights at every position independently.
keyPoints: Unlike self-attention, which explicitly relates different positions to each other, the feed-forward sublayer transforms each position's representation on its own, applying the exact same learned weights at every position independently.

questions.prompt: Why does a decoder's self-attention need to be masked, unlike an encoder's?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: A decoder generates text one token at a time, and shouldn't be allowed to attend to future positions it hasn't generated yet — masking enforces this left-to-right constraint

Since a decoder generates output sequentially, allowing it to attend to future positions during training would let it 'cheat' by looking ahead at what it's supposed to predict — masking explicitly prevents this, matching the real constraint the model faces during actual generation.
keyPoints: Since a decoder generates output sequentially, allowing it to attend to future positions during training would let it 'cheat' by looking ahead at what it's supposed to predict — masking explicitly prevents this, matching the real constraint the model faces during actual generation.

questions.prompt: What does BERT's masked language modeling (MLM) pretraining task involve?
questions.referenceAnswer: MLM masks a percentage of input tokens and trains the model to reconstruct them using the full bidirectional context surrounding each masked position — a task well suited to BERT's encoder architecture.
keyPoints: MLM masks a percentage of input tokens and trains the model to reconstruct them using the full bidirectional context surrounding each masked position — a task well suited to BERT's encoder architecture.

questions.prompt: What do scaling laws describe about language model performance?
questions.referenceAnswer: Scaling laws capture the empirical finding that language model performance follows a predictable pattern as three key factors — parameters, data, and compute — are scaled up, particularly when scaled together in balance.
keyPoints: Scaling laws capture the empirical finding that language model performance follows a predictable pattern as three key factors — parameters, data, and compute — are scaled up, particularly when scaled together in balance.

questions.prompt: What does a Transformer model's context length refer to?
questions.referenceAnswer: Context length (or context window) specifically refers to how many tokens a model can take in and attend to simultaneously in a single input — text beyond this limit needs to be truncated or handled with some other strategy.
keyPoints: Context length (or context window) specifically refers to how many tokens a model can take in and attend to simultaneously in a single input — text beyond this limit needs to be truncated or handled with some other strategy.

questions.prompt: How would you test that the change fixed this incident rather than hiding it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Keep a reproducible failing case for this incident. Compare a single sequence with its padded batch result. Compare the same workload before and after the change; record both the target metric and regressions.
